title: Wir haben Platz / Aufnahme von Geflüchteten demonstration, Vienna
location: Vienna: Karlsplatz procession to Heldenplatz; procession included stops at Greek, Croatian and Afghan embassies.
participants_original: Contemporary reports describe several thousand overall; CBA chronology says >1,200; ORF Wien attributes a peak estimate up to 5,000 to organizers. ORF national S001 instead says “yesterday” relative to 3 Oct publication (2 Oct), conflicting with ORF Wien, APA/Der Standard, the contemporaneous organizer call and CBA, all identifying 3 Oct. No police crowd estimate reported.
notes: Public call from Volkshilfe/Platform for Humane Asylum Policy demanded Austria accept refugees including people from Moria and addressed Austrian Chancellor/Interior Minister; event date coded 3 Oct based on converging local, APA and organizer dates, with S001 date conflict retained. No violence/state response established.

title: MAN Steyr warning strike and public protest march / assembly
location: MAN plant to Steyr Stadtplatz, Steyr, Upper Austria
participants_original: At least 4,000 according to works council/oe24-APA; around 5,000 per union GPA. Jobs figures (2,300 / 2,400 / 6,000 families) refer to affected employment, not crowd.
notes: Actual public street march and city-square works assembly are confirmed. Opened union/employer-related sources state primary demand as reversing MAN/VW closure and call on company/owner to keep jobs. GPA also criticized Chancellor and minister for not returning a works-council call; Upper Austrian councillor attended and pledged state-level efforts, but the protesters’ specific state-policy demand remains unresolved. Do not treat the politician’s presence/pledge as protesters’ request.

title: March for Life (Marsch fürs Leben), Vienna
location: Vienna city centre; Karlsplatz to Ringstraße / Heldenplatz and return
scope: City-centre march for Austrian abortion and end-of-life policy
organizer: Verein Marsch fürs Leben (reported by TFP; event organizer identity as described by Kathpress)
participants_original: Kathpress reports several hundred march participants; APA-OTS release reports 2,000 at Karlsplatz. OTS is organizer-originated; no independent exact crowd count found.
threshold_50_evidence: Kathpress contemporaneous report describes several hundred at the march; OTS organizer release reports 2,000. Both describe the same Vienna public march, not separate sites or pooled days; exact point/interval is uncertain.

start_date.value: Contemporaneous Kathpress report dated 17 October and OTS's 19 October release saying the march took place Saturday support 2020-10-17; later TFP organizer report says 19 October, retained as conflict.

end_date.value: Same-day march route returned to Karlsplatz in the contemporaneous report; the event is described as the Saturday march.

location.value: Vienna, beginning at Karlsplatz and crossing the city centre toward Heldenplatz and back.

organizer.value: Verein Marsch fürs Leben, as stated by TFP; Kathpress identifies organizers and associated ProLife Europe speakers.

participants.value: Several hundred, Kathpress report; 2,000, APA-OTS release; count origin is not independent/settled.

demands.value: The bishop called for retaining Austria's statutory ban on killing on request and assistance to suicide; event organizers sought support/counselling conditions for women and a three-day waiting period before abortion. These are domestic policy measures; OTS reports the march motto about protecting children and supporting women.

state_target.value: Austrian legal prohibition and abortion-policy framework; demands are directed toward Austrian law/policy.

protester_violence.value: unknown; no report establishing violence by march participants.

state_response.value: Police presence escorted participants; reports do not establish accommodation, arrests or use of force. Route disturbance is attributed to opposing demonstrators, not state action.

eligibility_basis.value: An executed public Vienna march in October is described contemporaneously; qualitative 'several hundred' supports the >=50 threshold, and speakers/organizers articulate Austrian abortion/end-of-life policy demands. Assignment day conflict and point-count uncertainty remain disclosed for reviewer determination.

notes: Likely single-day political march with domestic-policy target. Contemporary Kathpress report says 17 Oct and several hundred; OTS issued 19 Oct says 'Saturday' and 2,000, which also indicates 17 Oct. TFP's later organizer report gives 19 Oct, so the day conflict is explicit and unresolved. Do not treat OTS as independent turnout corroboration. Candidate remains pending distinct scientific review; no official coding/ID.
open_questions: Is TFP's 19 October event date a publication-date error, or does it refer to a separate action?
What exact attendance estimate did a non-organizer source independently observe?
Can a contemporaneous notice or independent report reconcile the 17/19 October discrepancy?
What specific bill or statutory process did the organizers address, beyond the general call to retain the current end-of-life prohibition and improve abortion-policy support?
